blocks.x: Retrieval that cites or refuses: permission-aware RAG over your regulated document estate, where every answer carries its sources, its freshness and its permission lineage — and where the corpus contracts that make that possible are built first, not last.
Why corpus engineering decides the answer quality

Retrieval-augmented generation done properly is corpus engineering wearing a chat interface. The model is the easy ten percent; the ninety percent is deciding what counts as truth in your estate, who may see it, how fresh it must be, and how an answer proves where it came from.

The organizational parts bite harder than the technical ones: document estates duplicate across portals, the authoritative copy is rarely the most recent one, and permission models live in systems the search team has never been allowed to read. We build the contracts that fix that first, because every grounded answer downstream inherits their quality.
Everything below is build-order material: the failure modes we design against, the architecture that fixes them, and the gates a release clears before a user sees an answer.
Four failure modes that quietly kill enterprise RAG
Each failure below has shipped in production somewhere; each has a countermeasure that lands with the build, not in a later phase.

blocks.caption: RAG & Enterprise Knowledge Systems: failure modes we design against — and the countermeasure that ships with the build
headers: What it looks like in production
rows: Stale authoritative sources
Answers cite a version of truth the owning team retired months ago
Freshness SLAs per source with owner paging at breach; answer carries source timestamp
Permission leakage
Retrieval returns documents the asker was never entitled to see
Query-time permission filter compiled from the source-of-trust ACL, tested in the eval suite
Duplicate and conflicting content
Six portals host three variants of the same policy; retrieval ranks the wrong one
Corpus dedup pass with canonical-source registry; conflicting pairs quarantined for review
Unmeasurable quality
Nobody can say whether last week's model change helped or hurt
Versioned eval suite with groundedness and citation precision thresholds blocking promotion

blocks.x: Reference architecture — permission-aware retrieval with citations

Two properties matter more than model choice here: nothing reaches the answer layer without passing the permission map, and every generated claim traces to a span in a source the asker was allowed to read. The lanes below show how those properties are enforced structurally rather than by prompt goodwill.

blocks.title: Reference architecture — permission-aware RAG with citations
blocks.note: The permission map filters at query time, not index time — index-time filtering rots the moment an ACL changes. Denied retrieval is logged with the reason code.

widgets.title: Retrieval stack progression — each stage's contribution measured
widgets.note: Click to isolate. Reranking buys 9 precision points for 600 ms — the latency budget decision is explicit and reviewed per feature class, not felt as a vague slowdown.

widgets.title: Chunk strategy what-if — size, overlap, top-k
widgets.note: The precision curve falls as chunks grow — big chunks retrieve the neighborhood, not the passage. Small chunks retrieve precisely but lose the argument. The overlap dial buys recall back at index cost.

widgets.title: The retrieval fabric — click nodes for their contract

nodes.label: Source estates
nodes.detail: SharePoint, Confluence, ticketing and document stores ingested with ownership metadata — every chunk carries who owns it and when it governs.

nodes.label: Chunking pipeline
nodes.detail: Semantic chunking with parent-document mapping; metadata enrichment (version, effective date, section) turns chunks into records.

nodes.label: Hybrid search
nodes.detail: BM25 + dense in RRF fusion; lexical catches identifiers, dense catches paraphrase — the fusion is measured, not faith-based.

nodes.label: Cross-encoder rerank
nodes.detail: Top-k reranked per query class; latency budget per class decides rerank depth — interactive and batch run different depths.

nodes.label: Scope filter
nodes.detail: Access control at retrieval time per query scope; the permissions model is the corpus model, enforced before generation sees anything.

nodes.label: Grounded generation
nodes.detail: Cited generation with refusal when evidence is absent; the persona never answers past its sources.

nodes.label: Groundedness harness
nodes.detail: Claim decomposition nightly: every sentence checked supported/unsupported/contradicted against retrieved evidence; scores published.

nodes.label: Citation store
nodes.detail: Answer citations with chunk lineage — the audit artifact that proves which document version answered the question.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read each contract. The scope filter sits before generation on purpose — permissions are enforced where the corpus is read, not where the answer is written.

blocks.x: The stack we default to — and when we deliberately leave it

Defaults exist so the first sprint spends its time on your corpus, not on bikeshedding components. Deviations are allowed where your estate argues for them; the conditions are written down so the deviation is a decision, not a drift.

blocks.caption: RAG & Enterprise Knowledge Systems: default stack and the conditions under which we deviate
rows: Hybrid retrieval
OpenSearch / Elasticsearch BM25 + bge/gte dense vectors
Single-stage dense when corpus is clean and small; lexical is never dropped entirely
Reranking
Cross-encoder reranker (bge-reranker class) on top-50
LLM-as-reranker only when the corpus is multilingual and the budget tolerates it
Vector store
pgvector when Postgres is already the system of record
Dedicated store (Milvus/Qdrant) only past ~50M chunks or sustained p99 pressure
Generation
Frontier API model, temperature pinned, JSON-constrained output
Self-hosted 8B–14B class when data residency forbids egress
Orchestration
LangGraph-class stateful runtime with typed state
Plain service code when the flow is a straight line — no framework tax
Citations
Span-level citation binding verified before render
Document-level citations only for regulatory narrative outputs
